bill.title: Stand Strong Falls Prevention Act
bill.latestActionText: Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions. Hearings held.
bill.officialSummary: Stand Strong Falls Prevention Act This bill establishes an advisory committee on falls prevention to assess federal efforts to prevent falls and recommend related policies to the Administration on Aging (AOA). The advisory committee must oversee the creation and maintenance of a national plan to address falls prevention, including through the advancement of programs or interventions to prevent falls and reduce the number and severity of fall-related injuries. The committee must also assist the AOA in coordinating falls prevention research and services across federal agencies. The committee must be comprised of members representing specified federal agencies, non-government organizations, and populations (e.g., caregivers and health care providers). Within a specified period, the advisory committee must submit an initial report to the AOA and Congress, including • an evaluation of all federally funded efforts related to falls prevention and recommendations for adjusting these efforts based on their purpose and performance; • a recommendation for developing a Medicare pilot or demonstration program to provide coverage for basic home modifications to reduce falls; and • recommendations for increasing provider use of a fall risk screening, assessment, and intervention tool developed by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. The AOA must submit regular reports to Congress with assessments of U.S. progress in addressing falls prevention, outcomes of the committee’s recommendations, and recommended priority actions. These reports must evaluate the implementation of any Medicare program initiated pursuant to a committee recommendation.

classification.plainSummary: This bill would create a federal advisory committee to coordinate falls prevention efforts across government agencies and develop a national plan to reduce falls among older adults. The committee would evaluate existing federal programs, recommend a Medicare pilot to cover home modifications that prevent falls, and encourage health providers to use CDC fall-risk screening tools. The Administration on Aging would report regularly to Congress on progress in reducing falls and implementing the committee's recommendations.

industries.rationale: The bill would promote provider use of fall risk screening and assessment tools, affecting clinical workflows and preventive care practices.
The bill recommends a Medicare pilot program to cover basic home modifications, which would expand covered benefits and affect claims and reimbursement.
A Medicare pilot covering home modifications to reduce falls would create demand for contractors performing accessibility and safety renovations.

plain.whatItDoes: This bill would set up an advisory committee on falls prevention to assess federal efforts to prevent falls and recommend related policies to the Administration on Aging.
plain.whoItTouches: People on Medicare. Anyone who buys health insurance.
plain.everydayEffect: If it passed, the change would show up in what Medicare pays for. Nothing has changed yet. Most bills never become law.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
